obs: Tree tunnel: dense rain-tree canopy over a 2-lane lane; cars parked both kerbs nose-to-tail; 4–5 storey 1920s–40s residential blocks. Facade view at same point: red-painted plaster (#A84A3C) with cream trim (#EFE6D2), arched ground-floor windows with keystones, timber balconies with fretwork brackets, louvred wooden shutters, sloped tin sunshades, compound wall low + iron railings with red/white pillars and ball finials, black heritage lamp post, interlocking pavers.

Back of Colaba Causeway toward Colaba market/Koliwada: 1-storey shacks with rusty corrugated roofs, political banner hoarding on poles, 30+ scooters/motorbikes parked in rows on a concrete open space, bougainvillea (magenta), rain tree, small 2–3 storey chawls in background, blue/white plastic tarps.

Quiet residential lane: 1950s 4–5 storey apartment blocks in cream/peach (#E8C9A8) with balconies closed by white grilles, AC units, compound walls painted white with steel gates, security cabins; canopy rain trees meeting over the road; red+grey paver footpath, round blue 'no parking' signs; parked cars one side; red car, scooters.

4-lane road with a ~2 m planted median (hedges + shrubs) whose kerb is painted BLACK-WHITE stripes; heritage triple-lantern black cast-iron lamp posts on the median every ~30 m; left: arcaded 4–5 storey blocks (white/cream #EDE6D6), BEST bus shelter (grey steel, ad panels), shop signs under arcade, grey paver footpath ~3 m; right: kaali-peeli taxis and cars parked angled at kerb, 5–6 storey Art Deco blocks with corner towers; rain trees both sides.

Victorian Gothic residence: buff stone/plaster darkened by monsoon (#C9B99A→#8E8270 streaks), pointed-arch ground-floor windows, carved timber verandah on upper floor with louvred shutters, small turret/gables, black iron railings on low stone compound wall, mature trees. (Old 2007 imagery.)

Modern 1980s–2000s apartment towers with tinted glass/teal paint (#3E7F7A), traffic signal on tall black pole (3 lamps + countdown), many areca and coconut palms in compounds, black steel railings, hedge planters, paver footpath, parked scooters, rain trees.

Wide 6-lane boulevard; raised median with BLACK-WHITE striped kerb, low hedge and shrubs; tall grey double-arm decorative lamp posts with globe lanterns on the median; long row of kaali-peeli taxis parked at the left kerb (taxi stand); black-yellow kerb blocks on footpath edge; big rain trees; Gothic/Edwardian stone buildings set back on left, Oval/maidan greenery on right.

Office-district service street: cars and kaali-peeli taxis (black body, yellow roof, tall-boy hatchback) parked on both sides and in the middle aisle; rain trees and palms; hedges along office plots; road-name signboard on a pole (blue, white text); 1970s towers set back behind trees.

street: Marine Lines flyover / Marine Drive north end
obs: Concrete flyover on round piers with blue-painted steel crash rails; corner petrol pump (orange canopy, parody brand needed); 4–5 storey cream corner building with ground-floor shop board; grey kerbs with low planters; scooters.

4+4 lanes of smooth dark asphalt, white dashed lanes, chevron hatching at slip merges; overhead sign gantry (blue/green boards); seaward side: low concrete sea-wall parapet + promenade, view of the curved bay; landward: raised island with BLACK-WHITE striped kerb + white railing, then a service lane; Art Deco 5–6 storey blocks with curved corners, horizontal bands, cream/white (#EFE9DC) and pastel green-grey (#D6DDD9), one building wrapped in GREEN construction netting + scaffolding (common sight); tall single-arm street lights; zebra crossings white on dark.

Looking west to Marine Drive: 2+2 lanes with a 2 m planted median (dense hedge) edged by BLACK-WHITE striped kerb blocks (~0.6 m each); grey twin-lantern decorative lamp posts in the median; Art Deco 5–6 storey blocks (cream, horizontal bands, curved balconies) left; restaurant cafés with awnings right; round revolving-restaurant tower at the Marine Drive end; cars + kaali-peelis parked both kerbs; big rain trees; overhead cable strung across.

Wide road, low green-verge median with plain grey kerb; buff Kurla-stone Gothic/Indo-Saracenic institutions (#CDB58A) with arcaded ground floors, pointed arches, bands of darker basalt, set behind iron railings; palms and rain trees; wide clean paver footpaths; very little shop clutter here (institutional stretch).

Continuous stone arcade (Gothic arches, buff stone with darker bands) on the west side — shops inside the arcade, book/hawker stalls; 4–5 storey Victorian commercial blocks; raised median planter (stone-clad, grey kerb) with royal palms and shrubs; kaali-peeli taxis parked along the arcade kerb; rain trees; very busy pedestrians.

Narrow 2-lane Fort street, 5–6 storey Edwardian blocks; banks with full-width red fascia boards and blue boards; cars parked tight both sides; delivery cyclists with cartons; tempo trucks; projecting blade signs; hawker under a blue tarp umbrella; overhead cables; rain-tree canopy at one end.

Quiet wide street under huge rain trees; single-storey heritage building with dark basalt rubble-stone walls and a sloped tiled roof, low boundary wall; 4–5 storey uniform Edwardian stone office blocks further on; cars parked angled; very few shops; staff parking.

Port edge: long white-washed concrete dock wall with Y-shaped posts and concertina barbed wire, grey concrete jersey barrier median (chipped, stained), white Tata-407-type box tempos and trucks parked on the kerb, delivery tricycle, coconut palm, 1–2 storey port sheds and shops with faded boards; dusty grey asphalt.

Busy bazaar arterial: orange-and-white plastic water-filled barricades as lane divider, a political flex banner with (fictional-to-be) leader portraits on the lamp post, white box sign 'BEAUTY SALON' and red/blue boards on a 3-storey timber-and-plaster building, blue direction gantry board, round no-entry and 'no right turn' signs, grey utility boxes on the footpath, kaali-peeli taxi, crowds walking in the road, rain trees further along.

Narrow canyon street (2 lanes, no median) between 4–6 storey old buildings; windows enclosed by rusty iron grille 'cages' and boxes, AC units stacked, tin sunshades; ground floor = wholesale shops with full-width blue/teal and red fascia boards (Devanagari + English), rolling shutters painted blue/grey; pedestrians walk in the carriageway; old kaali-peeli; overhead wires; one lone tree; worn asphalt with patches.

Two-lane trading street: Marathi/Gujarati shop boards (big red Devanagari lettering on cream boards), rolling shutters, 4–6 storey buildings with timber balconies and blue tarps tied over them; construction barricade of green mesh + yellow boards on the kerb, a white delivery tempo, motorbikes and cars parked; broken footpath with drain covers; rain tree at the far end.

street: Thakurdwar Road / Jagannath Shankarsheth Marg junction
obs: Metro/redevelopment works: BLUE corrugated metal hoarding sheets and green mesh fencing around a construction site (very common across South Mumbai now); weathered curved Art Deco corner building (grey-cream, stained), flex banner with a portrait on the signal pole, rusty grey electric feeder pillars on the footpath, stalls with tarp awnings, signal pole with countdown.

street: Maulana Shaukat Ali Road (Bhendi Bazaar end)
obs: Cluster redevelopment: 30–40 storey concrete towers under construction with tower cranes behind BLUE corrugated hoardings carrying notice boards; opposite side 4-storey weathered buildings with timber balconies, tin awnings and shops; crowds, handcarts and bikes in the road.

2+2 lanes with a low concrete divider painted BLACK-WHITE stripes; 6–8 storey 1960s concrete blocks with grilled balconies and many AC units; ground floor electronics shops with red/blue boards; tempo trucks and motorbikes parked along the kerb; multi-colour hawker umbrella; rain trees; tall towers behind.

Quiet 2-lane hill road with a dashed centre line, kerbs painted black-white; long beige stone/plaster compound walls (#D9C7A8) with pillars and wooden gates on one side, white compound walls with red-brick gate piers on the other; huge rain trees and banyans over the road; luxury apartment blocks (white) set back; very few people.

Narrow lane, 3–5 storey 1960s–70s buildings with curved balconies; vegetable sellers on the ground with produce on sheets, flower/puja shops with garlands, a temple with orange-gold dome on the right, plastic chairs and crates, blue tarps, a white sheet backdrop; pedestrians in the road; trees and creepers.

2+2 with a planted median (purple-flowering shrubs, hedges) and BLACK triple-lantern heritage lamp posts; 6–7 storey 1930s–50s plaster blocks (weathered grey-cream) with balconies and shops at ground; red BEST bus; yellow steel barricades with blue boards on the footpath; scooters parked; paver footpath with drain covers.

Wide 2+2 road without median; fruit handcart (bananas) under an umbrella; 4–5 storey older buildings with red shop boards and awnings; a 50+ storey glass residential tower behind; kaali-peelis, scooters, BEST buses; blue kiosk; rain trees on the far side.

3+3 lanes with a planted median (low hedges); BEST bus stop; 5–6 storey 1960s blocks, one tall tower wrapped in green netting; shop boards with dark fascias; pedestrians with umbrellas; rain trees along the footpath.

User-uploaded drive on an elevated deck: smooth concrete/asphalt, white dashed lanes, galvanised W-beam steel crash barriers on posts, blue-painted concrete parapet, tall single-arm lights, thick morning haze hiding the skyline.

2+2 lanes, planted median with BLACK-WHITE striped kerb; footpath kerb also black-white; 5–7 storey 1950s–70s apartment blocks (white/cream, monsoon-stained) with balconies; grey utility boxes, a red post box, painted compound-wall murals; palms and rain trees.

New elevated road on T-shaped piers with ORANGE-painted pier caps (#E07A2E) and concrete deck beside the road; BLACK-WHITE median kerb with hedges; college building with Marathi sign; hazy; tall towers behind.

Lively lane: rows of motorbikes parked, food stalls with umbrellas, political flex banner, 4–6 storey 1950s concrete buildings with grilles and shops, cars and taxis, big rain trees and a peepal; footpath with tiles; people everywhere.

Residential lane: 5–7 storey weathered chawl-type blocks (grey-cream, black stains) with iron grille boxes on windows; long row of scooters parked; cars along a yellow-painted boundary railing (school?); new towers behind; litter at the kerb; peepal tree.

Very narrow canyon lane (~6 m) between 5–6 storey buildings with iron grille boxes, timber balconies, green construction netting and laundry; shops with tin awnings; sacks, cartons and steel trunks on the ground; parked motorbikes; tangled overhead wires; a tempo blocking the far end.

Temple bazaar: white cloth canopy over a flower/puja stall, fruit and vegetable stalls on handcarts, garland sellers, big religious flex boards on the building above, blue tarps, mannequins outside a cloth shop, 4–5 storey old buildings painted pink-red (#C9605A) with grilles; dense crowds, women in saris, scooters.

Sloping lane with a basalt stone retaining wall; a construction plot enclosed by GREEN mesh netting with red-white barrier tape; 6–7 storey white apartment buildings with balconies and potted plants; big rain trees; a sentry/watchman cabin with a yellow roof.
